claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Fabric IQ brings three layers of business context into Microsoft IQ: unified data, business intelligence, and operational intelligence.
claims.quote: Fabric IQ brings three layers of business context into Microsoft IQ: [unified data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/overview#unified-data-with-onelake), [business intelligence](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/overview#business-intelligence-with-power-bi-semantic-models), and [operational intelligence](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/overview#operational-intelligence-with-ontologies).

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: An ontology is a machine-understandable business representation that defines entity types, properties, relationships, rules, and metrics, and binds them to live enterprise data so people, applications, and AI agents share vocabulary and context.
claims.quote: [Ontology (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/ontology/overview) is a shared, machine-understandable representation of your business. It defines entity types, properties, relationships, rules, and metrics, and binds them to live enterprise data so people, applications, and AI agents share the same vocabulary and context.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Fabric IQ provides structured grounding for copilots and agents so answers reflect enterprise language defined in the ontology.
claims.quote: Fabric IQ provides structured grounding for copilots and agents, so answers reflect your enterprise language as defined in your [ontology (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/ontology/overview).

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Ontologies can be created from scratch or generated from existing Power BI semantic models, carrying over calculated columns and source-owned DAX measures as metrics; details can also be generated by an ontology agent or imported from RDF or OWL.
claims.quote: You can create ontology items from scratch or generate them from existing Power BI semantic models to bootstrap from trusted logic already in production. This process also carries over calculated columns and source-owned DAX measures as metrics. You can also generate ontology details with the ontology agent or import them from open standards like RDF or OWL.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: With shared ontology language, agents can monitor live data, detect anomalies, and take governed action.
claims.quote: With this shared language, agents can monitor live data, detect anomalies, and take governed action.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: After ontology creation, a built-in graph model can be generated from entities, relationships, rules, and source bindings for relationship-centric questions.
claims.quote: After an ontology is created, you can optionally generate a built-in graph model from its business entities, relationships, rules, and source bindings to help answer relationship-centric questions.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The built-in ontology agent supports the ontology lifecycle through natural language, generating definitions and data bindings, answering business questions, and proposing changes for review under a proposal-first model.
claims.quote: The built-in ontology agent supports the ontology lifecycle through natural-language interactions: it generates definitions and data bindings, answers business questions against your ontology context, and proposes changes for your review under a proposal-first model.
